name: Cows and Primitive Roots
description: The cows have just learned what a primitive root is! Given a prime p , a primitive root is an integer x (1 ≤ x < p ) such that none of integers x - 1, x 2 - 1, ..., x p - 2 - 1 are divisible by p , but x p - 1 - 1 is. Unfortunately, computing primitive roots can be time consuming, so the cows need your help. Given a prime p , help the cows find the number of primitive roots .
input_specification: The input contains a single line containing an integer p (2 ≤ p < 2000) . It is guaranteed that p is a prime.
output_specification: Output on a single line the number of primitive roots .
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 284A — Cows and Primitive Roots [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
